description: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a culinary masterpiece, featuring succulent chicken marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic Indian spices, then cooked to perfection over hot charcoal. The charcoal grilling imparts an irresistible smoky flavor and a beautiful char, making each bite incredibly juicy and deeply satisfying. This classic Indian dish promises an authentic taste experience, perfect for a memorable dinner.

ingredients.notes: cut into 8 pieces, skin removed, deep slits made

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep slits all over the chicken pieces using a sharp knife. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply. Place the chicken in a large bowl.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In the bowl with chicken, add 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder. Rub this mixture well into the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the slits. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.

instructions.title: Second Marinade Preparation
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, combine the hung yogurt, remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, remaining 1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper powder, and the optional red food color. Mix well until a smooth, thick marinade forms. Stir in the mustard oil.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade to the second marinade bowl. Ensure each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or ideally overnight (12-24 hours) for best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marination, the better the result.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the hot coals on one side of the grill for indirect heat, leaving a cooler zone. Ensure the grill grates are clean and oiled to prevent sticking. The grill should be medium-hot.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals for a few minutes per side to get a nice char, then move them to the cooler side of the grill. Close the lid and cook, turning occasionally, for about 25-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165F (74C) and the chicken is cooked through and tender. Baste with any leftover marinade or a little oil during the last few minutes if desired.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the tandoori chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with lemon wedges, onion rings, and mint chutney. Enjoy this authentic charcoal grilled delight!

tips: For truly authentic tandoori flavor, ensure your yogurt is hung for a few hours to remove excess water, making the marinade thicker and more effective.
Kashmiri red chili powder provides vibrant color without excessive heat. If unavailable, use a mix of regular chili powder and a pinch of red food color.
Serve your hot tandoori chicken immediately with fresh lemon wedges, thinly sliced onions, and a cooling mint chutney or raita for a complete Indian meal.
article:
Mastering the art of Indian cooking at home can be a truly rewarding experience, especially when you bring the authentic flavors of the tandoor to your backyard. Among the myriad of Indian dinner recipes, Tandoori Chicken stands out as a global favorite, renowned for its vibrant color, smoky aroma, and succulent texture. While traditional Tandoori Chicken is cooked in a cylindrical clay oven known as a tandoor, we're going to dive into how you can achieve equally stunning results with a charcoal grill, imparting a unique depth of flavor that only live fire can deliver. Get ready to transform your dinner table with a dish that’s both impressive and incredibly delicious: Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken.

## What is Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken?

Tandoori Chicken is a classic Indian dish originating from the Punjab region, where whole chickens or pieces are marinated in yogurt and a blend of spices, then traditionally cooked in a tandoor. The high heat of the tandoor cooks the chicken quickly, sealing in juices while creating a beautifully charred exterior. When we talk about Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, we’re adapting this centuries-old technique to a modern backyard charcoal grill. The magic lies in the charcoal itself, which imbues the chicken with an irresistible smoky flavor that gas grills simply cannot replicate. The slow charring over hot coals creates a crispy skin and a tender, juicy interior, making it a perfect centerpiece for any Indian dinner. This method not only offers incredible taste but also an exciting cooking experience, bringing the essence of Indian street food and restaurant quality right to your home.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken

Creating authentic Tandoori Chicken begins with a robust marinade. Here’s what you’ll need:

For the Chicken:
*   1.5-2 lbs bone-in, skinless chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or breast halves work well)
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon salt

For the Marinade (First Marination):
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste

For the Marinade (Second Marination):
*   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt is excellent for thickness)
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1-2 teaspoons Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat) or regular chili powder (for more heat)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   ½ teaspoon black pepper
*   1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil or any neutral cooking oil
*   Red food coloring (optional, for authentic tandoori color)
*   Salt to taste (adjust after first marination)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Grilling

Follow these steps to prepare and grill your succulent Tandoori Chicken:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep gashes into the thickest parts of the chicken (2-3 gashes per piece) to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply.
2.  **First Marination:** In a large bowl, rub the chicken pieces with lemon juice, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours. This step tenderizes the chicken and lays a foundational flavor.
3.  **Second Marination:** While the chicken is marinating, prepare the second marinade. In a separate bowl, combine the yogurt, remaining ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, cumin, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, and kasuri methi. Add the mustard oil and a few drops of red food coloring (if using) and mix well until smooth.
4.  **Combine Marinades:** Drain any excess liquid from the first-marinated chicken. Add the chicken to the second marinade, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare the Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before you plan to grill, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange charcoal briquettes or lump charcoal for a two-zone fire – one side with direct high heat and the other with indirect medium heat. Allow the coals to ash over and reach a temperature of around 375-400°F (190-200°C). Clean the grill grates and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grilling Process:**
    *   Place the marinated chicken pieces over the direct heat zone of the grill. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, turning frequently, until you achieve a nice char and sear marks. Be careful not to burn the marinade.
    *   Once charred, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone. Close the grill lid and continue to cook for another 15-25 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) at the thickest part of the chicken, with no pink juices. Flip the chicken occasionally to ensure even cooking.
    *   For an extra smoky flavor, you can add a few wood chips (like mesquite or applewood) to the coals during the indirect cooking phase.
7.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum tenderness.

## Pro Tips for the Best Charcoal Grilled Results

Achieving perfect Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken every time requires a few insider tricks:

*   **Marination Time is Key:** Don't skimp on marination. The longer the chicken soaks in the yogurt and spices, the more flavorful and tender it will be. Overnight is truly best.
*   **Pat Dry Before Marinating:** Excess moisture on the chicken skin prevents the marinade from adhering properly and inhibits good browning. Always pat the chicken thoroughly dry.
*   **Use Bone-In, Skinless Chicken:** Bone-in chicken cooks more evenly and stays juicier. Remove the skin as it can become soggy and doesn’t crisp up well with the marinade.
*   **Achieve Two-Zone Heat:** This is crucial for grilling Tandoori Chicken. Starting with direct heat creates the beautiful char, while finishing on indirect heat ensures the chicken cooks through without burning the exterior.
*   **Monitor Temperature:** Invest in a good meat thermometer. Cooking to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) ensures food safety and prevents overcooking, which can lead to dry chicken.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Give each chicken piece enough space for even cooking and charring. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of grilling it.
*   **Scrape Off Excess Marinade:** Before placing chicken on the grill, gently scrape off any large clumps of marinade. While you want a good coating, thick clumps can burn quickly.
*   **Rest Your Chicken:** Just like any grilled meat, letting the Tandoori Chicken rest for a few minutes after cooking allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and moist final product.

## Serving Suggestions for Tandoori Chicken

Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a star on its own, but it truly shines when served with a selection of complementary Indian dinner recipes. Here are some classic pairings:

*   **Naan or Roti:** Warm, fluffy naan bread or whole wheat roti are perfect for scooping up the chicken and its flavorful juices.
*   **Mint Chutney:** A refreshing mint and coriander chutney provides a bright, tangy contrast to the rich, smoky chicken.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based dip, often with cucumber or onion, helps balance the spices.
*   **Kachumber Salad:** A simple salad of diced cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, and lemon juice adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Basmati Rice:** A side of fragrant basmati rice, either plain or jeera (cumin) rice, is always a welcome addition.
*   **Lemon Wedges and Sliced Onions:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the hot chicken brightens the flavors, and thinly sliced red onions offer a sharp, fresh bite.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is hard to beat, you can certainly experiment with variations:

*   **Paneer or Vegetable Tandoori:** For a vegetarian option, use cubes of paneer (Indian cheese), bell peppers, onions, and zucchini, marinating and grilling them in the same way.
*   **Fish Tandoori:** Firm white fish like mahi-mahi or cod can be marinated and grilled for a lighter, quicker-cooking alternative. Reduce grilling time significantly.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your preference for heat. For a milder version, reduce it; for more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Green Marinade:** For a different flavor profile, blend fresh coriander, mint, green chilies, and ginger-garlic paste with yogurt for a vibrant green marinade.
*   **No Charcoal Grill? No Problem!** While charcoal grilling offers the best flavor, you can still make Tandoori Chicken using other methods:
    *   **Oven:** Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25-35 minutes, then broil for 5-7 minutes to get some char.
    *   **Gas Grill:** Cook on a gas grill using indirect heat primarily, with a brief sear over direct heat for char.
    *   **Grill Pan/Skillet:** Cook chicken pieces on a hot grill pan or heavy-bottomed skillet on the stovetop, turning frequently until cooked through and nicely charred.

Whether you're a seasoned grill master or a beginner looking to explore new flavors, making Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is an incredibly satisfying culinary adventure. The smoky aroma, the tender meat, and the vibrant spices come together to create an unforgettable Indian dinner experience right in your backyard. So fire up your grill, gather your ingredients, and prepare to impress your family and friends with this truly spectacular dish!
